subject: mathematics
title: Bar-Graph Scouts
objective: Read a single bar graph and answer questions using its data.
introduction: Milo made a bar graph of his class’s pets. Can you use the title, labels, scale, and bar heights to read the data?

vocabulary.definition: The tallest bar in a graph shows the category with the most.
The shortest bar shows the category with the fewest.
Look at two bars to see which one is taller.

activities.instruction: Watch how labels, scale, and bar height reveal graph data.
activities.content: Read the title, labels, and scale. Compare bar heights, then use only the values shown in the graph.

feedback.retry: Read the title and labels before comparing any bars.

items.prompt: In a bar graph of class pets, the cat bar is the tallest. What does that tell you?

options.text: Nobody chose cats
Every pet in the class is a cat
Cats were chosen by the fewest children
Cats were chosen by the most children

items.explanation: The tallest bar shows the greatest amount, so the cat bar means more children chose cats than any other pet.

items.prompt: In the same bar graph, the fish bar is the shortest. What does that tell you?

options.text: Every child chose fish
Fish were chosen by the most children
Fish were chosen by the fewest children
Fish are not in the graph

items.explanation: The shortest bar shows the least amount, so the fish bar means the fewest children chose fish.

items.prompt: Milo wants to know whether more children chose dogs or birds. What should he do?

options.text: Count the bars in the graph
Compare the heights of the dog and bird bars
Read only the title of the graph
Guess without comparing the bars

items.explanation: To compare two categories, look at the heights of their two bars. The taller bar is the one more children chose.

items.prompt: A bar graph has the numbers 100, 200, and 300 on its scale. What do those numbers tell you?

options.text: The colors of the bars
The names of the pets
How many bars the graph has
How many children chose each pet

items.explanation: The scale numbers tell the amount each bar stands for. Match the top of each bar to the scale to read how many chose that pet.

items.prompt: In a bar graph of fruits, the mango bar is the tallest. Which statement is true?

options.text: The graph has no mangoes
Mangoes were chosen the most
Mangoes were chosen the least
No one chose mangoes

items.explanation: The tallest bar is the greatest amount, so the mango bar means mangoes were chosen by the most children.
